benchmarks.methodology: Scale Labs' April 2026 MCP Atlas evaluation. 1,000 human-authored tasks across 36 real MCP servers and 220 tools, with 500 public and 500 held-out tasks. Each task exposes 10–25 tools, usually 3–7 required tools and 5–10 distractors. A task passes when claim-level coverage reaches at least 75%; coverage is the mean of claim scores (0, 0.5, 1). The leaderboard metric is Pass Rate, evaluated in each model's default configuration without behavior-shaping system prompts. The updated harness permits up to 100 tool calls per task.

QBench preserves the 20 explicit table rows and does not claim a complete current leaderboard.

composite.name: QBench Index
composite.basis: Seven QBench capability families using eight source-audited evaluations. Scores retain publisher-reported 0–100 task-success or accuracy values; exact model/effort variants remain separate. ARC-AGI-3 Standard-harness results are included, while Provider Adapter is separate.
composite.normalization: For each eligible evaluation, retain its reported 0–100 percentage-point score. Average multiple evaluations within each family, then average the seven observed families equally. Evidence adjustment: Index = 50 + (Raw family mean − 50) × sqrt(Observed families / 7). This is not an IQ score or confidence interval.
composite.configurationPolicy: Create a separate model variant for each exact model name and reported reasoning effort. Never select the highest score across effort levels. Keep unreported effort separate. Preserve harness, routing, fallback, release date and model metadata. ARC-AGI-3 Standard and Provider Adapter are separate evaluations; only Standard contributes to the Index.

composite.method: QBench Index 1.3 uses eight source-audited evaluations across seven capability families. It retains publisher-reported task-success/accuracy percentages rather than converting within-cohort ranks to percentiles. Model/effort variants are separate identities. Ranking requires at least two eligible evaluations across two distinct families. Missing values are not imputed.
caveats: The Index is a seven-family composite of source-reported percentages, not an IQ score, human-equivalence score, or confidence interval.

Direct percentage-point scoring avoids within-cohort rank-percentile inflation. Benchmark difficulty, graders, task formats and guessing opportunities still differ; equal family weights are a transparent convention, not a psychometric equivalence claim.
Effort variants are separate rows. 'Not reported' means the publisher did not identify the reasoning effort; it is never inferred from a harness.
Harness differences are preserved. ARC-AGI-3 Standard and Provider Adapter are separate; only Standard contributes to the Index.
Coverage adjustment shrinks incomplete seven-family results toward 50. This is an evidence adjustment, not a confidence interval.

Ranking requires at least two evaluations across two distinct families to improve coverage without allowing single-benchmark results to become an Index rank. Rows with less evidence remain visible but unranked.
